![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14038597/assets/4c95243ea94951012ec14c6f16b4276a591c10c22798efc82f73bcd9d45e65ae.png)

What is the equation of the ellipse given above?

{{field-1}}$=1$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(-4,-1),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=5,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=4.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{{4}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.

Therefore, the major axis has length $2a=2\cdot 7=14,$ and the minor axis has length $2b=2\cdot \sqrt{7}=2\sqrt{7}.$

- Since $b^2=16,$ the length of the vertical radius must be $b=\sqrt{16} = 4.$

So the semi-major axis has length $a=5,$ and the semi-minor axis has length $b=4.$

Therefore, the major axis has length $2a = 2\cdot5 = 10,$ and the minor axis has length $2b = 2\cdot4 = 8.$
